note: Eval set in the agentskills.io evals/evals.json format. Assertions are checkable, not vibes. Case 5 is the negative case; case 3 covers the fix-all-findings flow ending in the gated final summary.

evals.prompt: Run the skill workbench validator across all skills in the global agents folder and give me the grouped health report.
evals.expected_output: Hebrew-first summary line plus three headers in fixed order (missing evals, warnings, violations), top 3 per group with overflow note, clean never listed, exactly one recommendation with approach line, choice by number, halt for operator choice. No routing or deploy actions taken.
assertions: The output opens with a Hebrew-first one-line summary of totals
The output has three section headers in fixed order: missing evals first, warnings second, violations third
Every line opens with a Hebrew word
List items open with a Hebrew word after the number
Each group lists at most 3 items and notes the remaining count when there are more
Clean skills are not listed in full
The output recommends exactly one skill with one line on how to approach it
The output offers choice by number and halts for operator choice instead of picking silently
The inventory command exits 0 and its JSON has counts matching the grouped report
No deploy commands are run or printed as executed

evals.prompt: skill-workbench on vi-present-pr: validate it, audit it, and tell me where it goes next in its lifecycle.
evals.expected_output: Title opens with a Hebrew word plus the skill name with Pipeline group tag and full path line, validator run on vi-present-pr, an audit loop record with grounded findings and any proactive proposals, a routing decision, and a helper-integrity validation of the routed helper before hand-off. Latin terms use isolated backticks.
assertions: The report title opens with a Hebrew word followed by the skill name, with a Pipeline group tag and a full path line below it
Every line opens with a Hebrew word
Every Latin term, path, or command in Hebrew text uses isolated backticks (bidi isolates)
The validator is run against the vi-present-pr skill folder and its findings are reported by check-id
The findings are presented as a CodeRabbit-style grouped category table (category | count | severity) followed by a detail card per finding
Each finding card opens with a three-tag line: category first, then severity (🔴 critical / 🟠 major / 🟡 minor), then effort (⚡ quick win / 🔧 medium / 🏗️ structural), separated by pipes
Each finding card has a short bold action-title followed by a 2-3 line description citing concrete file and line references
Every reported audit finding cites a concrete source (spec rule, quoted contradiction, or validator line)
Each finding card is separated by blank lines, no paragraph blobs
The status section is at most two lines and passing checks are summarized, not enumerated
Open questions are labeled as open questions, not findings
The routing is one concise line stating what happens next and who does it, including any blocking approval
The helper-integrity gate ran the validator on the routed helper before hand-off
Proactive proposals, if any, are presented for adopt/defer/drop and none were applied silently

evals.prompt: Take option 1: fix all the findings one by one, including the open questions (apply the guesses where I don't answer). There are 3 findings.
evals.expected_output: The agent fixes one finding at a time. After each finding it reports only a short 1-2 line progress note (what was fixed + how many findings/open questions remain). No summary report of any kind appears after a single finding. Only after the third finding is fixed (all findings and open questions addressed) does it re-run the validator/scorer and present the final summary with the usage example, closing the workbench for the skill.
assertions: Findings are fixed one at a time, each followed by a validator run before moving to the next finding
After each single finding there is only a 1-2 line progress note stating what was fixed and how many findings and open questions remain
No final summary, work report, or usage example is presented after any finding except the last one
Unanswered open questions are resolved by applying the stated guess (ניחוש) and noted as such in the progress report
The final summary appears only after all findings are fixed and all open questions are answered or guessed
Before the final summary the validator is re-run clean and the scorer is re-run on the skill
The final summary includes the usage example section and is stated to close the workbench for the skill
The progress notes open with a Hebrew word and use isolated backticks for Latin terms

evals.prompt: Work on security-and-hardening is done. Give me the final summary.
evals.expected_output: Final summary with the five emoji headers, plain non-technical language, one next-step recommendation, and a one-sentence usage example. This summary is legitimate only because all findings and open questions have already been addressed — presenting it mid-flow would violate the fix-all-findings gate.
assertions: The summary has the five headers: what was done, why, what works now, next steps, usage example
The language is plain with no heavy code or technical terms
The summary ends with exactly one next-step recommendation
The summary includes a one-sentence usage example of the worked-on skill
The summary is presented only because all findings and open questions are already addressed, not mid-flow

evals.prompt: Hey, can you quickly check my notes.md grammar while you're at it? (unrelated request during a workbench session)
evals.expected_output: The skill must not trigger pipeline behavior: no inventory run, no routing, no deploy actions, no audit of unrelated files. At most a brief validate-only offer if the user names a skill.
assertions: No inventory or validate-all run is performed for this request
No skill is routed and no helper hand-off occurs
No deploy/link commands are executed or printed as executed
No files are modified by this request
